name: continental_w670
label: Continental W670 10.9 L seven-cylinder radial (Stearman)

sources.what: Paul H. Wilkinson, 'Aircraft Engines of the World 1945', W-670 data page (p. 87): seven cylinders, single row, direct drive, not supercharged; bore, stroke, valves per cylinder, rating of 220 hp at 2,075 rpm.
Radial Engines, Ltd. parts catalogue and mechanics handbook (overhaul shop): compression ratio, firing order, valve timing at 0.124 in checking clearance.
Aircraft Engine Historical Society, 'Continental's Radial Aircraft Engines': Type Certificate 162 table (compression ratio, carburettor venturi 1-15/16 in), collector ring and stacks.
Wings of History Air Museum, R-670-5: firing order.

notes: Sourced: seven cylinders in one row, unsupercharged, bore, stroke, compression ratio, firing order 1-3-5-7-2-4-6, one inlet and one exhaust valve per cylinder, valve timing, carburettor venturi diameter, 220 hp at 2,075 rpm. No peak torque is published. The cylinder numbering direction is not stated by the sources; cylinders are placed so that this firing order gives even 102.9 degree intervals on the single crank throw. Valve timing is the overhaul handbook's (intake opens 4 after top centre, closes 21 after bottom centre; exhaust opens 49 before bottom centre, closes at top centre), which is measured with the valve clearance set to 0.124 in; that clearance is used here as the lift at which the events are quoted, so the seat-to-seat events come out wider. The real running clearance is 0.010 in cold, which would make the equivalent lift 0.114 in. The carburettor venturi (1-15/16 in, sourced) is put in as a 0.1 m pipe of that diameter ahead of the throttle (the `snorkel`), because the format has no venturi; the throttle bore itself (75 mm) is an estimate. The 2,075 rpm limit is the rated speed. Not modelled: the master rod and link rods (every cylinder has the same plain rod motion), and the propeller (the flywheel is the derived default, so it revs far more freely than the real engine). Estimated, not sourced: rod length, valve diameters (derived defaults), peak valve lift (0.5 in), idle speed, throttle bore, intake pipe length and diameter, plenum and airbox sizes, and the whole exhaust: seven short stubs into a collector ring with one short open stack and no muffler is typical of the type, but its layout and every dimension here are estimates (intake pipe length was tuned toward the rated power).
